subject: Renewal: EU primary + APAC standby onboarding and term amendment
messages:
From: Julia Kim <julia.kim@medinex.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-24T08:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal + EU primary / APAC standby question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we scope the renewal for July 1, Medinex would like to: 1) make EU the primary region for patient data residency; 2) add an APAC standby node for failover and peak-burst traffic during APAC hours; and 3) increase committed throughput by ~2x for the first 90 days of the renewal to support our onboarding spike.

Can you confirm if Redwood can: a) amend the current order to reflect EU residency as primary with onshore KV caching, b) guarantee cross-region failover latency SLOs, and c) provide the price delta for a temporary committed uplift (90-day ramp) vs a permanent reserved uplift? We also need any contract language that affects data routing, audit logs, and SOC-2 scope for EU primary.

We have the traffic profile attached and can share a Procurements contact for contracting redlines.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Kim
Head of Platform Operations, Medinex
Attachments: medinex-traffic-profile.csv (CSV)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Julia Kim <julia.kim@medinex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + EU primary / APAC standby question

Hi Julia — really appreciate the clear ask and the traffic profile, that helps a lot. Summary answers below and a next step to get terms drafted: 

- EU primary: Yes — we can set EU tenancy as the primary residency for all request paths and KV cache. We will enable onshore KV caching and audit-log retention scoped to EU region in the Private control plane.
- APAC standby: We can provision an APAC standby pool for warm failover and burst routing. Failover will be automatic by routing policy; cold start is avoided by warm standby.
- SLA / latency: For cross-region failover we guarantee a 95th percentile end-to-end failover latency of <300ms for warm failover paths. We'll include measurable latency buckets in the amendment.
- 90-day uplift vs permanent commit: We can offer a temporary 90-day committed uplift at ~1.3x the permanent reserved rate (reflects burst capacity scheduling), with an option to convert to a permanent reserved capacity at month-end one after the uplift. Exact pricing in the attached amendment draft.

I've attached an amendment draft that captures the data routing language, audit log retention specifics, and the uplift vs reserved pricing table. Next step: if this looks good we can loop in Legal and Procurement for a quick amendment + DocuSign signature.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) You sign the amendment as an interim addendum (DocuSign link to follow).
2) We spin up APAC standby in our staging pool and kick off a 2-week failover test window with your team.
3) If after 90 days you want a permanent commit, we convert with a credit for the uplift days.

Would Thursday at 10:00am CEST work for a short OKR/ops alignment call?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Account Lead — EMEA, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-eu-apac-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T13:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: Medinex uplift economics + credit policy

On Thu, Apr 25, 2027 at 09:40 Soojin Lee wrote:
> I've attached an amendment draft that captures the data routing language, audit log retention specifics, and the uplift vs reserved pricing table.

Quick sync for approvals: Medinex is asking for a 2x committed bump for 90 days (target onboarding). Our commercial recommendation is: offer the 90-day uplift at 1.3x reserved SKU pricing, with an option to convert to permanent reserved capacity. If they convert within 120 days, apply a pro-rated credit equal to 50% of the uplift premium days toward the reserved contract. 

Concerns/asks: 
- Ben: confirm capacity availability in APAC standby pool for May 15+; we may need to schedule a small capacity reservation to guarantee <300ms failover SLA.
- Legal: add explicit data routing clause that EU primary means all persistent storage & audit logs retained in EU region; ephemeral model cache may route to APAC for inference but KV/retention remains EU-bound.

I think the proposed credit gives them predictable economics while protecting our unit economics. Would like to approve the DocuSign go-ahead if Ben signs off on capacity.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-27T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: Medinex uplift economics + credit policy

Marissa / Soojin — checked infra and APAC standby pool can accommodate the 90-day 2x uplift starting May 10 with a small reservation of two GPU pods in apac-west-1. Operational notes: 
- We need a 5-day lead to warm caches and validate KV replication schedules.
- Will set up a failover test window (2 hours) with synthetic traffic to validate <300ms p95.
- There is a one-time configuration fee to enable onshore KV retention for EU primary (covers additional storage and audit log routing) — recommend we absorb half for partner goodwill on renewal and pass half to them.

If Marissa signs the commercial terms with that concession, I'll schedule capacity and prep runbook templates for the failover test.

Ben
Head of Platform Reliability
From: Julia Kim <julia.kim@medinex.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medinex.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@cloud-partner.io>
Date: 2027-04-30T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + EU primary / APAC standby question — acceptance

Soojin — this looks good and aligns with our legal team feedback. We accept the 90-day uplift at the proposed rate and the conversion credit terms. We also agree to split the KV retention configuration fee 50/50. Please send the DocuSign and we will have Procurement sign the amendment early next week.

A few operational asks before signing: 
- Can Redwood commit to a preliminary failover test before May 17 so we can confirm routing behavior?
- Please include the exact audit-log retention window (we asked for 7 years) in the amendment.

Thanks — will await the DocuSign link.

Julia
Head of Platform Operations, Medinex
